entities.name: Intervention-Oriented Expectations
entities.description: Intervention-oriented expectations predict divergent causal signs in ideology-contested cases.

entities.name: Market-Oriented Expectations
entities.description: Market-oriented expectations also predict divergent causal signs in ideology-contested cases.

relations.source: Ideological Bias in LLMs' Economic Causal Reasoning
relations.description: The study finds that LLMs exhibit systematic ideological bias when reasoning about economic causal effects.
The EconCausal benchmark is used to evaluate the accuracy of 20 state-of-the-art LLMs on their ability to predict empirically supported causal directions.
The study uses 10,490 causal triplets derived from top-tier economics and finance journals as the dataset for the EconCausal benchmark.
The study finds that intervention-oriented expectations are systematically more accurate than market-oriented ones in predicting empirically supported causal directions.
The study finds that across 18 of 20 models, accuracy is systematically higher when the empirically verified causal sign aligns with intervention-oriented expectations than with market-oriented ones.
The study finds that when models err, their incorrect predictions disproportionately lean intervention-oriented.

entities.name: Understanding and Mitigating Spurious Signal Amplification in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for Math Reasoning
entities.description: The paper focuses on addressing the issue of spurious signal amplification in test-time reinforcement learning for math reasoning.

entities.name: Test-time Reinforcement Learning (TTRL)
entities.description: TTRL is a technique that adapts models at inference time via pseudo-labeling, making it vulnerable to spurious optimization signals from label noise.

entities.name: Spurious Signal Amplification
entities.description: Spurious signal amplification refers to the phenomenon where responses with medium consistency form an ambiguity region and constitute the primary source of reward noise.

entities.name: Debiased and Denoised test-time Reinforcement Learning (DDRL)
entities.description: DDRL is a unified framework proposed to mitigate spurious signals, which consists of three stages: frequency-based sampling, debiased advantage estimation, and consensus-based off-policy refinement.

entities.name: Frequency-Based Sampling Strategy
entities.description: This strategy excludes ambiguous samples while maintaining a balanced set of positive and negative examples.

entities.name: Debiased Advantage Estimation with Fixed Advantages
entities.description: This stage removes the bias introduced by group-relative policy optimization using fixed advantages.

entities.name: Consensus-Based Off-Policy Refinement Stage
entities.description: This stage leverages the rejection-sampled dataset to enable efficient and stable model updates.

entities.name: Large Language Models
entities.description: The experiments are conducted on three large language models across multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

relations.description: TTRL is vulnerable to spurious optimization signals from label noise due to its pseudo-labeling mechanism.

relations.source: Debiased and Denoised test-time Reinforcement Learning (DDRL)
relations.description: DDRL outperforms existing TTRL baselines by mitigating spurious signals.

relations.target: Debiased Advantage Estimation with Fixed Advantages
relations.description: The frequency-based sampling strategy is combined with debiased advantage estimation to remove bias introduced by group-relative policy optimization.

relations.target: Debiased and Denoised test-time Reinforcement Learning (DDRL)
relations.description: The consensus-based off-policy refinement stage is a key component of DDRL that enables efficient and stable model updates.
The experiments are conducted on three large language models across multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks to evaluate their performance.

entities.name: MiMIC
entities.description: MiMIC is a method for mitigating visual modality collapse in universal multimodal retrieval while avoiding semantic misalignment.

entities.name: Universal Multimodal Retrieval (UMR)
entities.description: UMR aims to map different modalities into a shared embedding space for multi-modal retrieval.

entities.name: Marvel
entities.description: Marvel is an early-fusion approach that projects visual features into the language model (LM) space for integrating with text modality.

entities.name: UniVL-DR
entities.description: UniVL-DR is a late-fusion approach that encodes visual and textual inputs using separate encoders and obtains fused embeddings through addition.

entities.name: WebQA+
entities.description: WebQA+ is a dataset used for evaluating multimodal retrieval methods, where image in documents or queries might lack captions.

entities.name: EVQA+
entities.description: EVQA+ is another dataset used for evaluating multimodal retrieval methods, where image in documents or queries might lack captions.

relations.description: MiMIC addresses the challenges of visual modality collapse and semantic misalignment in UMR.
Marvel exhibits visual modality collapse, where it disregards visual features while depending excessively on textual cues.
Although UniVL-DR is less affected by visual modality collapse, it is more susceptible to semantic misalignment, where semantically related content is positioned far apart in the embedding space.
MiMIC outperforms Marvel in multimodal retrieval tasks.
MiMIC consistently outperforms UniVL-DR in multimodal retrieval tasks on the WebQA+ and EVQA+ datasets.

entities.name: Remote Sensing Infrared Image Super-Resolution (x4) Challenge
